name: Nathu La
image_query: Nathu La pass India China border

local_name.name: Nathu La
local_name.meaning: Traditionally 'the listening ears pass'; 'la' means pass

tagline: The India–China border pass at 4,310 m
meta_description: Nathu La guide: Indians-only permit rules, open days, 2026 cab fares, altitude advice and the pass's history from the Silk Route to the 2006 trade reopening.
summary: Nathu La is a mountain pass at 4,310 m on the India–China border, about 54 km from Gangtok. Indian nationals can visit with a permit arranged a day ahead, usually Wednesday to Sunday, combined with Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir. Foreigners are not allowed. Snow often closes it in winter.
intro: Nathu La crosses the Dongkya range between Sikkim and the Chumbi Valley of Tibet, about 54 km east of Gangtok on NH310. For centuries it was one of the main trade routes between Tibet and India: mule trains carried wool, salt and borax south and cloth, grain and manufactured goods north. It was sealed after the 1962 war and reopened for border trade on 6 July 2006.

Today, Indian visitors drive up from Gangtok through Tsomgo, past Baba Mandir, to a parking area just below the border. From there, steps lead to a viewing area where Indian and Chinese posts face each other across the wire. Army staff manage the site, and the atmosphere is disciplined. Visits are short, usually 30–45 minutes, because of the height and the security rules.

Nathu La is open only to Indian nationals, with a permit of about ₹200 per person applied through a registered agent a day ahead, with ID and photos. It is usually open Wednesday to Sunday and closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and snow can close it for days between December and March. At 4,310 m, altitude sickness is a real risk. Check current status before you travel.

story.title: Forty-four years shut, reopened in July 2006
story.text: In 1873 the British official J.W. Edgar surveyed Nathu La and recorded a busy trade over it. Thirty years later, in 1903–04, Francis Younghusband's expedition to Lhasa used Nathu La and the neighbouring Jelep La, and Nathu La became the main communication route between India and Lhasa. Mule caravans used it until the Sino-Indian war of 1962, when the pass was sealed. In September 1967 it saw serious clashes between Indian and Chinese troops, followed on 1 October by fighting at Cho La, a few kilometres north. For 44 years nothing crossed. Then, on 6 July 2006, India and China reopened Nathu La for border trade, with marts at Sherathang on the Indian side and Renqinggang on the Chinese side. Since 2015 it has also been a route for Indian pilgrims on the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra. Trade volumes have stayed modest, limited to certain days and to the warmer months.
story.source: Wikipedia: Nathu La; Nathu La and Cho La clashes

little_known.fact: Since 2015, Nathu La has been one of the two official routes for the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra organised by India's Ministry of External Affairs; the route is motorable most of the way.
little_known.source: Wikipedia: Nathu La; Kailash Mansarovar Yatra

little_known.fact: Nathu La is one of the official Border Personnel Meeting points where Indian and Chinese army officers hold scheduled meetings and ceremonies.
Border trade through Nathu La takes place only on set weekdays and only in the warmer months, roughly May to November, through the Sherathang trade mart below the pass.

facts: India–China border, Silk Route history, snow
Indian nationals only; ≈ ₹200 via registered agent, a day ahead

highlights.title: Standing on the border
highlights.text: From the viewing area you look directly across to Chinese border posts a few metres away, with the Chumbi Valley dropping beyond. Few places in India put you so close to an international border. Photography rules are set by the Army on the day; follow them exactly.

highlights.title: The Silk Route's old crossing
highlights.text: Mule caravans used Nathu La for centuries, carrying wool and salt south and cloth and grain north. The 1903–04 Younghusband expedition crossed here. Standing at the top in the wind, it is easy to see why the trade only ran in the warmer months.

highlights.title: Snow from October to May
highlights.text: Nathu La is often snowbound from late autumn to spring, and even in May there can be drifts beside the road. For many Indian visitors it is the highest point they have ever stood. Bring warm, waterproof layers and sunglasses.

highlights.title: Sherathang trade mart
highlights.text: Below the pass, on the road up, is Sherathang, the Indian trade mart opened when border trade resumed in 2006. Traders with special permits cross from here on trading days. It is a reminder that this is still a working border, not just a viewpoint.

highlights.title: A full day of high places
highlights.text: Nathu La is usually combined with Tsomgo Lake (3,753 m) and Baba Mandir (about 4,000 m) in a 7–9 hour day from Gangtok. It is a long, high day, so we keep the pace gentle, with tea stops and enough water.

how_to_reach.text: Shared tours to Tsomgo, Baba Mandir and Nathu La run from Gangtok on open days, with seats sold by agents for about ₹1,200–1,800 per person including the shared vehicle. You must hand in ID and photos the day before. Only Indian nationals can join the Nathu La part.

A reserved SUV from Gangtok for Tsomgo, Baba Mandir and Nathu La costs about ₹6,500–9,000. Only Sikkim-registered tourist vehicles with the right permit can go up. Leave by 7 am; permits require you to start back by early afternoon.

Nathu La is a day trip from Gangtok only. You need at least one night in Gangtok to get the permit, which is issued the evening before, and to acclimatise. Allow 4–5 hours from Bagdogra or NJP to Gangtok on NH10, which closes in the monsoon. Check current status before you travel.

costs: Reserved SUV, Tsomgo + Baba Mandir + Nathu La
where_to_stay: There is no accommodation near Nathu La for tourists. Stay in Gangtok and go up for the day. Central hotels make the 7 am start easier: Hotel Tibet, The Chumbi Residency and Elgin Nor-Khill are all close to the taxi pickup points, and Mintokling Guest House and Hotel Sonam Delek suit budget travellers. If you want to sleep high on a separate trip, the Old Silk Route homestays at Kupup, Gnathang and Zuluk in Pakyong district are open to Indian nationals with a Silk Route permit.
tips: Nathu La is for Indian nationals only; foreign members of a group must stop at Tsomgo or Baba Mandir.
It is usually closed on Mondays and Tuesdays and after heavy snow; plan it for a Wednesday to Sunday.
Spend at least one night in Gangtok first, walk slowly at the top and stay no more than 30–45 minutes.
Carry original ID; the Army may check it at the top.
Photography rules change; never photograph troops or installations unless told you may.

experiences.title: Visit the border at Nathu La
experiences.cost: Permit ≈ ₹200; included in circuit car fare
experiences.summary: Climb the last steps at 4,310 m to the viewing area where India and China face each other across the pass. A short, disciplined visit run by the Army, and the high point, literally, of most Sikkim trips for Indian travellers.
body: Cars stop at a parking area below the pass. From there it is a short walk and a flight of steps to the viewing area. At 4,310 m, those steps feel like a mountain: go slowly, pause often and let children and older relatives set the pace. Army staff guide visitors, check permits and explain the rules for the day.

At the top, the border runs along the ridge. Chinese posts and buildings sit just beyond the fence, and on a clear day you can see down into the Chumbi Valley in Tibet. Prayer flags and memorial plaques line the Indian side. The wind is strong and cold even in summer.

Visits are kept short for safety, usually 30–45 minutes. Photography rules vary: sometimes it is allowed towards the scenery, sometimes not at all, and never of troops or installations. Ask before raising your phone. Nathu La is for Indian nationals only and usually open Wednesday to Sunday. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Which days is Nathu La open for tourists?
faqs.a: Nathu La is usually open to Indian tourists from Wednesday to Sunday and closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. It also closes after heavy snow, for security reasons and on some national occasions. Your agent will confirm the day before when applying for the permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can foreigners go to Nathu La?
faqs.a: No. Nathu La is open to Indian nationals only. Foreign travellers, including OCI cardholders, are not allowed beyond the points their permit covers, usually Tsomgo and Baba Mandir. Mixed groups can travel together, with foreign members waiting at Baba Mandir while Indians continue.

faqs.q: Can children visit Nathu La?
faqs.a: Older children in good health usually manage a short visit, but 4,310 m is very high, and very young children cannot tell you when they feel unwell. We advise against taking children under about five. For all children, keep the visit short and watch for drowsiness, vomiting or unusual crying.

experiences.title: Sherathang and the reopened trade route
experiences.summary: A short roadside stop at Sherathang, the Indian trade mart below Nathu La that opened when border trade resumed in July 2006 after 44 years. It puts the old Silk Route history into a present-day context.
body: When India and China reopened Nathu La for trade on 6 July 2006, two marts were set up: Sherathang on the Indian side, below the pass, and Renqinggang on the Chinese side. Registered traders from Sikkim, holding special trade passes, carry an agreed list of goods across on trading days, and Tibetan traders come the other way.

For visitors, Sherathang is mostly a glimpse from the road: low buildings, trucks and, on trading days in the warmer months, traders with bundles. Ask your driver whether a short stop is allowed on the day; rules depend on security conditions. Do not photograph officials or installations.

The trade is small compared with the old caravans, limited by weather, the agreed goods list and the season. But it continues a route that carried wool, salt and borax south and cloth and grain north for centuries, and that Younghusband's men marched over in 1903–04. It is worth a few minutes of your attention.

faqs.q: Can tourists buy goods at Sherathang trade mart?
faqs.a: Generally no. Sherathang is a border trade mart for registered traders with special passes, not a tourist market. Visitors can see it from the road and sometimes stop briefly. For Tibetan and Chinese goods, look in Gangtok's Lal Bazaar and the shops around MG Marg instead.

faqs.q: When did Nathu La reopen for trade?
faqs.a: Nathu La reopened for border trade on 6 July 2006, after being closed since the 1962 war, a gap of 44 years. Trade runs through the Sherathang mart on the Indian side and Renqinggang on the Chinese side, on set days during the warmer months.

faqs.q: Is Sherathang on the way to Nathu La?
faqs.a: Yes. Sherathang lies on the road up to the pass, a short distance below Nathu La. Most cars pass it without stopping. If you are interested, ask your driver whether a brief stop is possible on the day; it depends on security rules and traffic.

experiences.title: Tsomgo, Baba Mandir and Nathu La in a day
experiences.best_time: Wednesday to Sunday, April–June and October–November
experiences.summary: The full high-road day from Gangtok: Tsomgo Lake at 3,753 m, Nathu La at 4,310 m and the Baba Harbhajan Singh shrine, back by late afternoon. How to order the stops, pace the altitude and avoid the common mistakes.
body: Hand your ID and photos to your agent by midday the day before. Leave Gangtok around 7 am, after a light breakfast. The drive to Tsomgo takes about two hours with the permit check. Many drivers go straight up to Nathu La first, to reach the border before cloud and wind build, and then stop at Baba Mandir and Tsomgo on the way down.

That order also helps with the altitude: you spend the least time at the highest point and descend steadily through the afternoon. At Nathu La keep to 30–45 minutes. At Baba Mandir, around 4,000 m, take tea and visit the shrine. At Tsomgo, walk slowly by the lake before the last two hours back to Gangtok.

A reserved SUV costs about ₹6,500–9,000. Carry water, snacks, warm layers, sunglasses and cash. If anyone develops a severe headache, vomiting or confusion, descend at once. Nathu La is for Indian nationals only and usually closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does the Tsomgo, Nathu La and Baba Mandir trip take?
faqs.a: Allow 7–9 hours from Gangtok, leaving around 7 am and returning by about 3–5 pm. The time depends on traffic, the permit check, snow and how long you stay at each stop. It is a long day at altitude, so plan a quiet evening afterwards.

faqs.q: Which is better: Nathu La first or Tsomgo first?
faqs.a: Many drivers go to Nathu La first, to reach the border before afternoon cloud and wind, then visit Baba Mandir and Tsomgo on the way down. This also limits time at the highest point. Your driver will decide on the day based on permits, weather and traffic.

faqs.q: What if Nathu La is closed on our day?
faqs.a: If Nathu La is closed for snow or security, you can usually still visit Tsomgo and Baba Mandir on the same permit. The car fare is lower without Nathu La. If Nathu La matters to you, keep a spare Wednesday to Sunday in your plan.

experiences.title: Snow at Nathu La in April and May
experiences.summary: For families travelling in the summer holidays, April and May are the best months to find snow at Nathu La while the road is usually open. Snow walls beside the road, white slopes and clear mornings, with fewer closures than midwinter.
body: In midwinter, from about December to March, Nathu La often closes after snowfall, sometimes for days. By April and May the road is usually cleared, yet deep snow remains beside it and on the slopes around the pass. For families from the plains travelling in the school holidays, this is often the best chance to see real snow.

Mornings are usually clearer, with cloud building after noon. Daytime temperatures at the pass are around freezing to a few degrees above, with strong wind. Hire gumboots and coats at Tsomgo on the way up for about ₹100–300, and carry gloves, a warm hat and sunglasses.

May and June are also the busiest months, with long queues of cars at the check post. Get your permit early and leave Gangtok by 7 am. Snow can still fall in spring and close the pass at short notice. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there snow at Nathu La in May?
faqs.a: Usually yes. In most years snow remains beside the road and on the slopes around Nathu La into May, while the road itself is cleared. Exact conditions vary by year. Fresh snowfall is possible even in late spring. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the temperature at Nathu La?
faqs.a: In winter it falls far below freezing, often -10 °C or colder at night. In April and May daytime temperatures are around 0–8 °C with strong wind. In October and November expect 0–10 °C on clear days. It always feels colder than the number because of wind.

faqs.q: Do we need snow boots at Nathu La?
faqs.a: Waterproof boots help in snow season. If you do not have them, gumboots can be hired at Tsomgo stalls for about ₹100–300. Long padded coats and gloves are available too. Ordinary trainers soak through quickly and can lead to very cold feet at 4,310 m.

faqs.q: Who can visit Nathu La?
faqs.a: Only Indian nationals can visit Nathu La, with a permit of about ₹200 per person arranged through a registered agent a day ahead with ID and photos. Foreigners, including OCI cardholders, are not allowed. Check current status before you travel, as rules change with security conditions.

faqs.q: How do we get a Nathu La permit?
faqs.a: Give your registered agent or hotel a government photo ID and two passport photos the day before, usually by midday. The agent applies, and the permit is issued in the evening together with the Tsomgo permit. You cannot apply yourself at the pass. Carry the original ID on the day.

faqs.q: How high is Nathu La?
faqs.a: Nathu La is at 4,310 m (14,140 ft). That is high enough for altitude sickness in people who come up quickly from the plains. Sleep at least one night in Gangtok first, walk slowly, keep the visit short and descend if anyone feels very unwell.

faqs.q: Is Nathu La open in winter?
faqs.a: It is officially open on permitted days, but snowfall often closes it between December and March, sometimes for several days. April to June and October to November are the most reliable months. Keep a spare day if Nathu La is important to you. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a Nathu La trip cost from Gangtok?
faqs.a: A reserved SUV for Tsomgo, Baba Mandir and Nathu La costs about ₹6,500–9,000 per car in 2026, plus permit fees of about ₹200 for Nathu La and ₹200–400 for Tsomgo per person. A shared seat on the same circuit costs about ₹1,200–1,800. Prices are indicative.

faqs.q: Can we photograph at Nathu La?
faqs.a: Rules are set by the Army on the day. Sometimes scenic photos are allowed, sometimes all photography is banned. Never photograph soldiers, bunkers or installations. Ask before taking out a phone or camera, and delete images if asked. Drones are strictly prohibited.

faqs.q: Is Nathu La safe for senior citizens?
faqs.a: Many fit seniors visit without trouble, but 4,310 m puts real strain on the heart and lungs. Anyone with heart disease, high blood pressure, COPD or recent surgery should consult a doctor first. Use the steps slowly, keep the visit short and carry any regular medicines.

faqs.q: What is the history of Nathu La?
faqs.a: Nathu La was a major Tibet–India trade route for centuries and was used by the 1903–04 Younghusband expedition. It was sealed after the 1962 war, saw clashes in September 1967 and reopened for border trade on 6 July 2006. Since 2015 it has also served Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims.

faqs.q: Can we visit Nathu La and Tsomgo on the same day?
faqs.a: Yes, that is the standard plan. Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir and Nathu La are on the same road, and one permit request covers all three for Indian nationals. Allow 7–9 hours from Gangtok. The trip is usually possible Wednesday to Sunday.
